about: Content pairs for Reader's layered deduplication gate (plan row 9). Every text is invented (fictional companies and figures), because the repository is public. Each pair says what it IS (expect: same|different) and which layer should decide it (layer: url, identity, fingerprint, or model). A pair marked 'model' must NOT be merged by the free layers (they may only pass it on or say different); the paid check asks the model about those and nothing else. Doubt always means different: a duplicate shown twice is visible and fixable, a story merged away is not. Written by the autopilot run of 2026-10-20/21; every pair is a judgement, which is why the set needs Varun's sign-off before row 9 is DONE.

a.title: Helio Labs releases Orbit 1.0
a.text: Helio Labs released Orbit 1.0 on 14 October 2026, an open-source SDK that lets developers run several coding agents against one repository without them overwriting each other's work. Orbit gives every agent its own working branch and merges the results through a review queue, so a human sees one combined change instead of five competing ones. In the company's internal trial across 212 repositories, the queue reduced merge conflicts from 31 percent of runs to 9 percent. The SDK is licensed under Apache 2.0 and ships with adapters for three agent frameworks. Helio says the trial measured only repositories under 2 million lines of code, and it has not tested monorepos. Pricing for the hosted queue starts at 40 dollars a month per team, while the SDK itself is free to self-host.

a.title: Beacon is in public preview
a.text: Beacon is Northwind Labs' managed vector index for retrieval-augmented applications. It stores embeddings, filters them by metadata and returns the closest matches through one API call. The service is billed per query and per gigabyte stored, with no minimum commitment. Customers can export their data at any time in an open format, and deleting an index removes its backups within thirty days. Northwind publishes its security practices, its uptime history and the full list of regions on its trust page, and every release goes through the same review process before it reaches customers. Beacon entered public preview on 9 June 2026. During the preview the index supports up to 5 million vectors per customer and runs in two regions, and Northwind makes no uptime commitment. Early testers reported query latency of about 80 milliseconds at the 95th percentile on a 1 million vector index. Northwind expects the numbers to change before general availability.

b.title: Beacon is generally available
b.text: Beacon is Northwind Labs' managed vector index for retrieval-augmented applications. It stores embeddings, filters them by metadata and returns the closest matches through one API call. The service is billed per query and per gigabyte stored, with no minimum commitment. Customers can export their data at any time in an open format, and deleting an index removes its backups within thirty days. Northwind publishes its security practices, its uptime history and the full list of regions on its trust page, and every release goes through the same review process before it reaches customers. Beacon became generally available on 21 October 2026. The index now supports up to 500 million vectors per customer, runs in seven regions and carries a 99.9 percent monthly uptime commitment. Northwind measured query latency of 35 milliseconds at the 95th percentile on a 10 million vector index and says the preview limits have been removed.

a.title: Sparse Probes
a.text: Cobalt researchers propose Sparse Probes, a method for locating which layers of a language model store a given fact. Probes trained on 4,000 traces find the relevant layer for 83 percent of tested facts. The method needs no fine-tuning of the base model and adds under 1 percent to inference cost. It is evaluated on one model family at three sizes and on English text only. Acknowledgements. This work was supported by the Cobalt Institute for Machine Intelligence. We thank our colleagues in the evaluation group for discussions and the reviewers for their comments. All experiments were run on the institute's shared cluster. Ethics statement. The study uses only public datasets and involved no human participants. The authors declare no competing interests. Code and trained weights will be released under a permissive licence after review.

b.title: Draft Reuse
b.text: Cobalt researchers study Draft Reuse, a way to speed up speculative decoding by recycling rejected draft tokens. On a benchmark of 1,200 prompts the technique raises throughput by 1.4 times with no change in output quality. The gains shrink on prompts longer than 8,000 tokens, and the evaluation covers a single hardware configuration. Acknowledgements. This work was supported by the Cobalt Institute for Machine Intelligence. We thank our colleagues in the evaluation group for discussions and the reviewers for their comments. All experiments were run on the institute's shared cluster. Ethics statement. The study uses only public datasets and involved no human participants. The authors declare no competing interests. Code and trained weights will be released under a permissive licence after review.

a.title: Lakeside opens its cache
a.text: Lakeside has opened its shared cache to outside developers after months of internal use. Union representatives said they had not been consulted before the news broke.
